feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: clear positioning, relevant progression, and solid domain expertise. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but impact is reduced by repetition, limited quantified outcomes beyond one role, and a slightly crowded skills structure.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level brand: the headline, summary, and career progression align well around digital strategy, communications leadership, and platform modernization.  
- Strong credibility: NACo progression shows advancement and increasing scope; tools/platforms listed support the claims made in experience.  
- Generally polished writing: no obvious misspellings; grammar is strong and tone is consistent, with concise, professional phrasing.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes across roles: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results. Include metrics on engagement, growth, efficiency, campaign performance, or cost/time savings.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT.” Consolidating these sections would improve structure and scannability.  
- Tighten style consistency: use serial commas consistently (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); consider “12 years of experience” instead of “12 years experience”; “A2/Learning” is slightly awkward—use “French (A2, currently learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV, but it is slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. It would be stronger with sharper positioning, cleaner phrasing, and one or two more distinctive qualifiers tied to recent leadership-level work.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, more standard phrasing.
- Lead with current senior value proposition: digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with tighter grouping such as “multi-channel digital communications.”
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving multi-channel communications, platform modernization, and content operations for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital strategy, web governance, editorial workflow design, and stakeholder coordination. Strong background in advocacy and public-sector messaging, translating complex technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content and scalable digital systems.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/systems language overlap heavily with Core Competencies.
- Advocacy messaging and stakeholder coordination are reinforced repeatedly in skills sections; keep the intro high-level.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. It would be stronger if tightened around distinctive, senior-level capabilities and phrased more consistently.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms like “Multi-channel communication” with more senior, specific phrasing such as “Cross-channel communications leadership.”
- Align wording with the strongest evidence in recent roles: “CMS modernization,” “Editorial governance & workflow design,” “Analytics & performance reporting,” and “Advocacy & policy communications.”
- Remove softer competency phrasing like “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” unless reframed as “Cross-functional leadership” or “Stakeholder alignment.”
- Possible rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Cross-channel communications leadership • CMS modernization & web operations • Editorial governance & workflow design • Analytics & performance reporting • Workflow architecture & process improvement • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the header.
- “Web & CMS administration” and “Data analytics & reporting” overlap with Topline Skills/Technical + IT; use sharper, higher-level phrasing to differentiate.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear relevance to your positioning, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and NACo entries. Tighten it around distinctive consulting impact, named deliverables, and any measurable scope.

Suggested edit
- Open with client scope + value: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Replace generic bullets with sharper outcomes/deliverables, e.g. “Built Drupal microsites, modular campaign components, and member toolkits to support advocacy and storytelling initiatives.”
- Consolidate technical execution: combine CMS/front-end/troubleshooting into one bullet and add scale if possible (“for X public-facing sites,” “serving X users,” “reduced turnaround time by X%”).
- Make the AI/search bullet more outcome-led: “Led AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content model, and discovery UX for complex policy/member content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, and enterprise web improvement” repeats language already used in the summary and NACo roles.
- The microsite/AI search bullets overlap with Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and let projects hold the detail.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals. It would be sharper if the opening line were less broad, bullets were more outcome-focused, and channel-management points were de-duplicated against the earlier NACo role.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the summary with a tighter scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management, leading platform modernization and organization-wide communications operations.”
- Rewrite bullets to emphasize outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where possible for email/social/video/analytics: growth %, engagement lift, production savings, reporting time reduced, faster publishing, fewer governance issues.
- Tighten wording: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing internal capacity for advocacy programming, event production, and recurring multimedia content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; focus this entry on leadership, modernization, analytics, governance, and budget ownership.
- Video capacity-building may overlap with older NACo bullets; keep this version strategic and outcome-based, not operational.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize what you owned at this level: newsletters, video cadence, and cross-team editorial operations.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to clarify scope and level: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial coordination.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions:
- Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing a repeatable policy communications channel.
- Coordinated editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams to improve alignment and publishing consistency.
- Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve efficiency and content quality.
- If possible, add metrics: open/click rates, video views, production volume, turnaround time, or stakeholder/team count supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Led digital communications across web, email, social and video” is too close to the Director role; use “managed day-to-day operations” instead.
- Video/livestream language also overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; keep this entry focused on scaling the recurring advocacy series.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Make it sharper, more senior, and more distinctive by emphasizing enterprise leadership and governance rather than generic communications phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with tighter, less repetitive bullets:
- Enterprise digital strategy and platform modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing systems and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership for complex organizations
- Public-sector and advocacy content strategy
- Audience-centered planning, messaging and user journeys
- Consider swapping “multi-channel communications leadership” for “cross-channel communications operations” only if you want closer alignment with recent roles.
- If space allows, add one stronger differentiator such as “AI-enabled content discovery strategy” to reflect current consulting work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” repeat language already used in the header and Core Competencies.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is broad and low-impact compared with the stronger governance/modernization themes elsewhere.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it’s too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent strengths rather than repeat a full software list.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a laundry list to grouped capabilities: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • Web modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and discovery”
- Drop lower-priority or older items unless they are target-role keywords; keep Drupal first, as it is most supported by recent experience.
- Remove “jQuery” from this topline section unless the role specifically asks for it; it reads dated and is already implied by front-end implementation.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “Enterprise CMS modernization and migration” to better reflect the 10,000+ page Drupal migration.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; avoid repeating WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, and Airtable in both sections verbatim.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; consider keeping it in only one place.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section and reads as a tool list rather than a senior, outcomes-oriented capability summary. This section should emphasize strategic analytics leadership over platform repetition.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first, e.g.:
- Analytics strategy and measurement frameworks
- KPI design and executive reporting
- GA4, BigQuery, Power BI and Looker Studio
- User behavior analysis, SEO and performance optimization
- Consider replacing “Microsoft Clarity” with “user behavior analysis” unless Clarity is especially important for target roles.
- Tighten “Leadership reporting” to “executive reporting” for clearer, more standard phrasing.
- If space allows elsewhere, connect to impact with a short qualifier like “for enterprise web and campaign performance.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization.”
- Repeating all analytics tools here may also echo the NACo Director role bullet about expanding analytics infrastructure.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies plus multiple NACo bullets. Make it tighter and more senior by emphasizing production leadership and delivery environments rather than basic tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Delivery”
- Replace with tighter, higher-level phrasing:
- Broadcast and advocacy video production
- Livestream and hybrid event delivery
- In-house studio and PTZ camera operations
- Virtual event production and technical coordination
- If space allows, add one scope cue tied to recent work, e.g. “broadcast-quality in-house studio production” or “recurring advocacy programming”
- Avoid “video production and editing” if editing is not a differentiator versus broader leadership/operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies; consider keeping the broader phrase there and making this one more tool/format-specific.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” and “Livestreaming” are partially redundant; combine for concision.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” section. This item should either be tightened or made more specific to platform depth/recent use.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: Drupal (enterprise migration, modular microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, order by relevance/recency: Drupal • Power Pages • SharePoint • WordPress • GitHub Pages
- Consider adding level cues instead of just names: Drupal (advanced) • WordPress (working) • SharePoint/Power Pages (working) • GitHub Pages (basic)
- If you want more impact, swap GitHub Pages for a more strategic qualifier: Drupal CMS modernization • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills; keep one list broader and the other more outcome- or proficiency-focused.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight versus the seniority of the rest of the CV unless tied to a specific use case.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and newer tools that support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API and tag implementation • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the CV uses versioning consistently elsewhere; they add little value.
- Consider replacing broad terms with sharper phrasing: “API integrations” → “REST/API integrations”; “GitHub Actions” → “CI/CD automation with GitHub Actions.”
- If accurate, add one outcome-oriented qualifier tied to recent work elsewhere, e.g., “front-end implementation for Drupal microsites” or “serverless scripting for web automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing.
- GTM may also overlap with analytics/tooling; keep it here only if positioned as implementation, not reporting.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too broad and reads like an undifferentiated software list. Since workflow automation is already a core competency, make this entry more intentional by emphasizing systems you likely used to build processes, not just collaborate.

Suggested edit:
- Split into two clearer groups to show depth: “Automation & Workflow: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier” and “Project/Team Operations: Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Teams.”
- Remove Basecamp unless it was meaningfully used in recent roles; it feels older/less relevant than the rest.
- If space allows, add a light qualifier in the heading: “Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Systems” to better match the tools listed.
- Prioritize tools tied to impact in recent roles; lead with Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier rather than project-management platforms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating all three sections with the same emphasis.
- Slack and Teams are generic workplace tools; keep only if you need keyword coverage.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful tools to include, but this line is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses the strategic email/engagement depth shown in recent roles. Tighten the label and, if possible, signal scale or platform ownership rather than listing brands only.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, strengthen with scope: Enterprise email campaign platforms for newsletter, member communications and engagement journeys
- Best option if space allows: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp | newsletter operations, audience segmentation, automated journeys

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating generic “email newsletters” language already covered in NACo roles unless you add something new here, such as segmentation, automation, or platform administration.
- Don’t overstate Mailchimp if it was minor compared with Dynamics 365 or Higher Logic; order tools by recency/importance.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs or scale if you can add them.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add specific scope/results where possible: website refresh size, livestream/event volume, video cadence, audience reach, or workflow improvements.
- Tighten the second sentence around 2–3 core contributions: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and improved day-to-day digital publishing workflows.”
- Replace “high-impact” and “strengthening” with evidence-based language; change “providing day-to-day guidance” to “supervised/mentored one digital media associate” if accurate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this item as launching or establishing the format.
- Avoid repeating broad channel coverage already stated in later NACo entries unless tied to first-team/buildout context.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads broadly and undersells the most distinctive achievement: launching NACo’s first podcast. Since later roles already cover digital/media growth, this item should emphasize foundational innovation, cross-functional coordination, and first-of-its-kind execution.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to lead with the standout result: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county policy and program priorities, while expanding NACo’s early digital content capabilities.”
- Make the podcast achievement more concrete: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Tighten “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” to something more active, e.g. “Produced digital and multimedia content to support organizational programs and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scope or output: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, or audiences/program teams served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating later-role language about video, editorial workflows, or digital operations; those are already stronger in 2015–2024 entries.
- Don’t overstate leadership/team management here; keep it as a coordination-and-launch role.
